name: Khalifa Belqasim Haftar
role: Commander of the eastern-based Libyan Arab Armed Forces
summary: Haftar advocates a unified Libyan state with a powerful army acting as a political guarantor. His later electoral commitments coexist with a record of claiming military authority and repressing opponents; he supports a role for Islamic law alongside civil legislation.

sources.title: Exclusive interview, Diaries of a Correspondent – 700 Days in Benghazi (2025)
sources.author: Khalifa Haftar, interviewed by Ahmed Ibrahim Amer
sources.usedFor: Latest extensive self-description; electoral rules, armed forces, sovereignty, reconstruction. Sympathetic interviewer; claims of battlefield conduct are not independently established.

sources.title: The Libyan Arab Armed Forces: A network analysis of Haftar’s military alliance (2021)
sources.author: Tim Eaton, Chatham House
sources.usedFor: Military political authority, commercial expansion and centralized personal networks.

sources.title: Khalifa Haftar: My forces will reach Tripoli soon (2014 interview)
sources.author: Khalifa Haftar, Asharq Al-Awsat
sources.usedFor: Own acknowledgement of directing forces attacking Congress, opposition to national division and targeting the Brotherhood.

sources.title: Haftar: We are sons of Sharia (2014 radio interview excerpts)
sources.author: Khalifa Haftar; reported by Osman Sassi, Al-Wasat
sources.usedFor: His distinction between definitive Islamic rules, contemporary interpretation and civil legislation.

sources.title: Libya’s Haftar says he has mandate from the people for military to take control (2020)
sources.author: The National
sources.usedFor: Public declaration accepting military rule and rejecting the Skhirat agreement.

sources.title: Take-no-prisoners speech, transcript reproduced in Trump Endorses U.S. Citizen-Turned Libyan Warlord (2019)
sources.author: Khalifa Haftar; translation and analysis by Ryan Goodman, Just Security
sources.usedFor: Speech permitting all weapons and rejecting capture of prisoners; primary transcript distinguished from legal commentary.

sources.title: Hold commanders of Tariq Ben Zeyad armed group accountable for catalogue of horrors (2022)
sources.author: Amnesty International
sources.usedFor: Investigated record of repression by forces subordinate to the LAAF; no assumption that each subordinate crime was personally ordered.

sources.title: The Private Sector amid Conflict: The Case of Libya (2020), overview note 7
sources.author: Aminur Rahman and Michele Di Maio, World Bank
sources.usedFor: Haftar’s October 2017 decree extending military authority into service and manufacturing projects.

sources.title: Haftar sets August deadline for fair distribution of oil revenues (2023)
sources.author: Moataz Wanis, Anadolu Agency
sources.usedFor: Regional oil-revenue demands; not evidence for general equal outcomes or equal ownership.

sources.title: Khalifa Haftar Calls for Unity and Libyan-led Solution (2025)
sources.author: LibyaReview
sources.usedFor: Later insistence on domestic sovereignty and military guarantee of political agreements.

strong-leader.rationale: His 2020 acceptance of a mandate for military rule bypassed the existing civilian political arrangement.

state-harmful.rationale: He describes the state as society’s protective shield and guarantor of rights.

empower-police-military.rationale: He calls for continual expansion of army training, equipment and capabilities.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He insists the political settlement come from Libyans rather than externally designed initiatives.

revolution-justified.rationale: He endorses the 2011 uprising and describes returning to support change as a national duty.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He extended the military investment authority’s mandate over manufacturing and service projects.

democracy-best.rationale: His 2025 support for unrestricted popular choice conflicts with his record of claiming military authority.

right-to-secede.rationale: He explicitly rejects division of Libya, calling it a single unit.

political-violence-never.rationale: He acknowledges directing the armed operation against Congress and defends his wider military campaign.

separate-church-state.rationale: His proposed legal framework retains binding Islamic rules rather than strict separation.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He supports Sharia on definitive matters alongside civil laws in other areas.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His take-no-prisoners instruction removes ordinary protections from internal enemies; later claims of humane treatment contradict it.

people-in-arms.rationale: His project replaces fragmented armed formations with a professional national army.

elective-rulers.rationale: He demands a president directly elected by Libyans in free and fair elections.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He explicitly presents military involvement in politics as necessary to protect the army and state.

suppress-opposition.rationale: His declared campaign targets Brotherhood members, while investigations document systematic repression of perceived LAAF critics.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He treats building a permanent professional army as an indispensable national task.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He says every era requires interpretations to be taken into account, while preserving definitive Islamic rules.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He justifies the Tripoli campaign as disarming militias and restoring national armed authority.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: In 2025 he defines democracy through free popular choice and competitive presidential and parliamentary elections.

no-business-privileges.rationale: His decree gave the army special commercial authority over enterprises in its territory.

notes: Whole-career review includes 2011 uprising, 2014 congressional assault, 2017 economic decree, 2019 Tripoli offensive, 2020 military-mandate declaration and 2025 interviews. Later electoral statements are recorded rather than erased by his earlier conduct; unresolved contradictions receive low confidence. Theme searches covered economy, government, society, world, liberty, culture, ecology, technology, means and globalism. No direct positions located for most welfare, family, minority-rights, environmental or technology propositions. Reconstruction promises do not establish universal healthcare; oil revenue sharing does not establish general equality of outcomes. Travel restrictions issued by al-Nadhouri and statements by Haftar’s sons are not automatically attributed to him. Command-linked abuses are attributed as investigated, not treated as adjudicated personal criminal liability. No living-person inferences.
